verdict: Alphabet's revenue rose 16% to $102.3B as Google Cloud grew 34% — and a $12.8B paper gain on its equity stakes lifted net income 33% to $35.0B, even after a $3.5B European fine.

segments.name: Google Services
segments.note: Search, YouTube, subscriptions and devices. Search revenue grew 15%, YouTube ads 15%, and subscriptions, platforms and devices 21%.

segments.name: Google Cloud
segments.note: Cloud computing for businesses — growth of 34% on enterprise AI infrastructure and AI solutions, and operating profit nearly doubled to $3.6B.

segments.name: Other Bets
segments.note: Moonshot projects like Waymo self-driving cars; they lost $1.4B at the operating level.

segments.name: Hedging losses
segments.note: Losses on Alphabet's currency-hedging program, which exists to smooth out exchange-rate swings on its overseas revenue.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineers and AI research; up 22% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling ads and cloud contracts, and marketing Google's products.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back-office, legal and admin costs — including the $3.5B European Commission fine.

otherDetail: A net gain of $12,759M, primarily net unrealized gains on non-marketable equity securities — stakes Alphabet holds in private companies.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Cloud is surging
takeaways.text: Google Cloud revenue jumped 34% to $15.2B and its operating profit nearly doubled to $3.6B, driven by enterprise demand for AI infrastructure and AI solutions.

takeaways.title: A European fine sat in the costs
takeaways.text: Operating income includes a $3.5B European Commission fine. Excluding it, operating income rose 22% and the operating margin was 33.9%, helped by strong revenue growth and a leaner expense base.

takeaways.title: Capex guidance raised again
takeaways.text: Alphabet raised expected 2025 capital spending to $91-93B, up from $85B, as Cloud customers' demand strains capacity. Third-quarter capex was $24.0B and free cash flow was $24.5B.

oneTimers: Operating income includes a $3.5B charge related to the European Commission (EC) fine, recorded within general and administrative expenses. Excluding the fine, operating income increased 22% and operating margin was 33.9%.
Other income includes a $12.8B net gain, primarily net unrealized gains on non-marketable equity securities (stakes Alphabet holds in private companies).
